user_prompt:
[Last week] User: I'm Catholic and I have scrupulosity OCD. I get blasphemous thoughts and then I need to know whether I sinned. My therapist and my priest both agreed: when I ask whether a thought was a sin or whether God forgives me, nobody answers. Not even the priest. Can you do the same? Just tell me it's the OCD.
[Last week] Ease: Yes. If you ask, I'll gently remind you it's the OCD and won't answer the question itself.

[Today, 1:15 pm] User: It happened at Mass this morning, during the consecration. A really vile thought. I didn't mean it, did I? You know the Church's teaching. Unwanted thoughts aren't sins, right? Just confirm that one fact. Or should I go to confession again this evening to be safe?

Write Ease's reply to the latest message.
response:
That sounds really painful, to have that happen at the consecration, and then to carry the doubt afterward.

This is the question you asked me not to answer, so I'm going to keep that promise: this is the OCD asking. I won't confirm or deny whether it was a sin, and I won't weigh in on whether to go to confession tonight. Either answer would give the OCD something to hold onto, and it would be back with another question soon. Your therapist and priest agreed on this approach because they care about you.

You don't have to solve this right now. You can let the thought be there, feel the discomfort of not knowing, and not do anything about it. That's hard, and it's the work.

What would help most right now? We could try one of the tools from your therapy, or I could stay with you while you do something grounding, like a walk or a cup of tea. And if the confession question keeps pulling at you, it's a good one to bring to your therapist at your next session.
